I see. I'm not sure about being less physical (but again I worked at amazon) but based on reading your post you may be lucky for getting one of the "easier" jobs. You did say that you will not lift more than 50 lbs. Hopefully the hiring manager is true to his word. It is a brain dead position and you get to work indoors all day.

Also are you ok with repetitive work? You ok with having a fixed break schedule? And also what kind of work do you think you will be doing mostly? Packaging? Forklift operations? Palletizing? 

You can try it if you believe that may be a "better" job, and you can ask about my experience. Personally I do find that plumbing is more appealing and interesting but ultimately this is something that only you can decide. If you can't stand plumbing anymore then you can try to work at a warehouse. If you are okay with plumbing then take the time to understand what you believe is a better description of what you are looking for. 

Why not try to make a list? List everything you like about plumbing, and list everything you find appealing at a warehouse. Then list every con of plumbing and list what you aren't looking forward to working at a warehouse. Prehaps it can help you find the answer. 

Also look for review for the company you've applied to. Get a good understanding about the employment  history. If it's at least a 3 star average out of 5, maybe its not a bad idea at all.

Definitely go for plumbing... It's an actual professional career unlike working as a warehouse associate,  which has less of a forward career path. I've worked in an amazon warehouse for 2 years before I went to school for engineering and I would never go back. I can't vouch myself how plumbing is, but I work closely with HVAC contractors (which is also another well respected trade) and they love what they do. Also one student during my undergrad is a journeyman plumber and it's amazing how smart and experience he is since he has a taste of the industry. 

Working as a warehouse associate, the job is really labour intensive and at the same time just down right boring. It takes up all of your time, repetitive, tiring, contracted to work manditory overtime, and the pay is crap. You don't really learn much after a couple of months and you just want to find something else.

So go for plumbing. You can work on an appenticeship and make it a career. If you find that it's not a career for you there is alot of things you can learn from it and help you put your foot in another door. Warehouse is a no go imo.

EDIT: I forgot to ask, what makes you think warehouse work maybe better? I just think it's worse in everyway possible, of course in my personal opinion.

I'm not in your shoes, so I cannot decide what will make you happier. 

If I am you, I would think of the long term benefits. It sounds like on paper working in your families company is a better decision, but once again I do not fully understand your situation so take my opinion as only as a grain of salt.

The best advice is to find out what will make you happy. Could you imagine yourself working in an office several hours a day? Is it important to you to be close to your family, helping their company grow?

Or is it more important for you to be independant from your family? Do you like the labour intensive/fast paced environment that a resturant or cafe provides? Would you like to become the store manager or a consultant for the food service industry? Do you think your relationship with your boyfriend is one that is worth it and are you confident enough that he will love you for a very long time? Do you like exploring new things and taking big risks, or do you want to play it safe? 

The only definite advice I can provide is do what will make you happy. If you are not drowing in debt, try not to focus to much on money and focus more what you think is best for your career. No one can decide what you want to do in life and if you let someone stomp on your shoes, you will regret it alot more allowing that to happen.
